Definitely worth buying.[/td] [/tr] [/table] [i]When I first dived into Be My Horde, I expected a standard top-down action roguelike game. But what I experienced was an exhilarating conquest of domination that made me feel like the ultimate force of evil![/i] [h1][b]📝Story/Plot without spoilers:[/b][/h1] In Be My Horde, you step into the shoes of Moriana, a mysterious and powerful necromancess determined to decimate the living. Little is known about her true motivations, but one thing is clear – every enemy that stands in her path becomes a resource to fuel her growing army. As you battle waves of brave warriors, foolish peasants, and even explosive sheep, the ultimate question remains: How big can your horde become, and how long can you hold your ground before the relentless waves overwhelm you? [h1][b]🎮Gameplay:[/b][/h1] [b]First Impressions-[/b] At the heart of Be My Horde lies an innovative twist on the horde survival genre. Unlike most games where enemies are mere obstacles, here they become your most valuable resource. With every creature that falls, Moriana can resurrect it and turn it into a loyal minion. These minions then fight at your command, creating a unique and satisfying loop where enemies feed your power. This core mechanic drives the game’s dynamic nature, making each playthrough feel fresh and rewarding. [b]Necromancy as Resource Management-[/b] The game challenges you to think strategically about which enemies to prioritise for resurrection. Do you bolster your horde with sheer numbers using weak peasants, or do you save your energy to raise stronger units like knights or cavalry? The beauty of the game lies in the freedom to experiment with different combinations and find the synergy that best suits your playstyle. [b]Dynamic Horde Evolution-[/b] The more you play, the larger and more diverse your undead army becomes. Each type of unit has distinct traits and abilities—knights can shield your weaker units, cavalrymen can charge at enemies, and the infamous exploding sheep can clear out entire groups. This variety forces you to adapt as you progress, ensuring the gameplay doesn’t stagnate. On each run, you’ll unlock new abilities and minion types, making your horde feel unique every time. One of the highlights is the quick, fast-paced gameplay that makes it perfect for short bursts or extended sessions. Runs can last anywhere from a few minutes to over an hour, depending on how well you manage your army. The satisfaction of watching your tiny group of undead minions grow into a massive horde capable of overwhelming the screen is indescribable. [b]Roguelike Progression and Dark Domain-[/b] Between battles, Moriana retreats to her dark domain, where she can use the souls of fallen enemies to upgrade her skills and powers. This roguelike progression allows you to gradually unlock new abilities, such as faster summoning times, more resilient minions, or enhanced necromantic spells, and more overall health that can decimate large groups of enemies. The dark domain also features unlockable structures that provide passive buffs, offering multiple layers of customisation. The progression is satisfying and keeps you coming back for "just one more run." [h1][b]📷Graphics:[/b][/h1] The art style perfectly blends the dark and grim tone of necromancy with a splash of vibrant visuals. The 2D graphics are clean and detailed, allowing you to distinguish between different enemy types and minions at a glance. The animations of both living and undead characters add to the visual appeal, making each battle chaotic yet delightful to watch. The environments themselves evolve as Moriana’s dark magic spreads, turning once-bright fields into cursed, barren lands – a beautiful yet eerie transformation. [h1][b]📝Main Pros and Cons:[/b][/h1] [b]Pros-[/b] [list] [*]Satisfying horde-building mechanics. [*]Fluid and immersive combat. [*]Haunting yet appealing graphics and audio design. [*]Endless replayability thanks to various upgrades and strategies. [/list] [b]Cons-[/b] [list] [*]A few more enemy types can benefit the gameplay. [/list] [h1][b]🏷️Tips to new players:[/b][/h1] Focus on upgrading Moriana’s core abilities early on to improve survivability. Be it regenerating health, having aura that damages enemies nearby or getting a speed boost when you barren a tree, sometimes it's better to dodge the ambush. The game is designed to have more and more runs; failure is just the beginning! [h1][b]😇Honest Rating:[/b][/h1] The game is genuinely fun to play. The balance between horde management, upgrades, and the sheer thrill of commanding a legion of undead minions makes it an absolute delight. If you’re looking for something fun and engaging, this game is a no-brainer. Totally recommended for all fans of fast-paced, strategic gameplay! Rating: 9.5/10 Time to raise my own horde.

[h2]You can put lipstick on a mistress …[/h2] When faced with the Survivors-Like genre it is an ordeal to stand out. The landscape of games where the screen is crowded with enemies are a dime a dozen. Therefore it is refreshing to see a game that has the idea to just take the dead enemies and make them your own army. Necormancy is perfect for this. [h3]A likeable entry in the genre[/h3] As with all Survivors-Like games, if there is a story it doesn’t matter. That might be another point where a survivors-like game has the chance to stand out, if it manages to tell a compelling story. With this game you don’t have that. You play as a minion in the service of an evil mistress, that controls the mistress in the levels?! The writing has double entendres where the mistress is being cheeky with her choice of words, i.e. when knights with lances show up, she says something along the lines of size matters, regarding the lances. Thankfully it’s only cheeky and overall forgettable. The voice acting is superbly done for a game in this price-range. The music is spectacularly fitting for the setting. The further you progress into a stage, the more intense the music gets, which adds to the atmosphere of blood and carnage on the battlefield. The graphic style is chosen wonderfully, although there are a few elements, where there is dialogue between two characters it looks like a washed up version of Hades sadly, i.e. the eyes of the mistress are too big for her head. Sadly, with all that the game has going on for itself, we have yet again developers who don’t understand the essence of the genre. [h3]The cold hard truth[/h3] The grind is not the fun part of these games. The fun part is the power fantasy. I really wish, that developers of this genre will get this fact. In the case of this game it’s even more blatant how the developers try to stretch the game time. Every stage has it’s own kind of souls, that are used to develop the progressions systems. While that is a staple of the genre, and a necessay condition I’d argue, it baffles my mind, that the developers think it’s a good idea to bind resources of the hell stage to only usable perks in the hell stage. And to top that, it’s painfully obvious, that the progression is scaled in a way, that you can only go far enough to buy one perk at a time. The predictability of this sucks out all the fun. Regarding the hell stage: While it is refreshing to see, that the stages get harder, I don’t see the reason why a survivors-like game has to have tactics, the likes of: „I need to get these skills so I can have enough minions to tackle that pack beacause I need X minions to kill Y of those … .“ And so on. All the more frustrating when you are severly limited by banishes and rerolls, for some reason. [h3]… but that doesn’t make her desirable[/h3] Be My Horde frustrates, because the ideas for a good game are there, the foundation is set. But it is hindered by counterproductive decisions and a misguided understanding of what the genres core-identity is, that it’s a part of.

I am writing this review because i kind of get irritated every time i see this in my library. Not because the core game is bad or the game-play loop is ♥♥♥♥. The core stuff is good and what it should be. The reason i do not recommend it, is that I do not understand how in the world a dev team manages to add so little content to game in such a long time. This is basically right click to necromance+. But right click to necromance was build in 48h by a team. This game has been in development for way longer that that and I just cannot for the live of me understand why nothing is happening. They have such a good basis and no new content / new mechanics / features. Nothing. And the roguelike element of this game, as it is right now, might aswell not exisit at all. Its useless almost. You cant just call your game a "roguelike" because you give the player about 20 powerups over 30+ mins which all boil down to something like: "Do all little bit of more damage", "Move a little bit faster" etc...... Nothing noteworthy there, like jesus christ I am sure some guys in the team spend some effort on this but really? This is the extent of your creativity..... I am pretty sure they just put the simplest stuff the could think of into the game to be able to put "roguelike" into the tags. Anyone who has played it will probably agree with me that that element of the game might as well not be there....... Please, just add content you have such a good base and going at a slow rate like this is just hurting you, nothing has been moving. And also please rework your powerup system, its trash. (Also they kind of deliberately tried to prolong game time by making the released hell mode ultra hard, so that you had to farm forever for upgrades. They claimed they just got the difficulty wrong because "our team plays it so much we know all the tactics and how to get strong fast so we thought it was not that hard" which in my opinion is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ XD. They just cranked the difficulty unreasonably high to keep people playing by needing to grind upgrades to finish hell mode)

There is no reason it takes more than 2 seconds to kill the most base level peasant. Not the knights, priests, cavalry. Not them. Just the peasants. YOU CAN REMOVE 75% OF THEIR HEALTH AND IT'D STILL BE VIABLE. It's just annoying. Is it just to eat time? Because it's not like I have any abilities to press. So what? I just stand still instead of exploring, opening more graves, whatever? I BEAT THE FIRST LEVEL AND THEN GET IMMEDIATELY CRUSHED ON THE 2ND LEVEL AND HAVE TO GO BACK TO GRIND THE FIRST LEVEL OVER AND OVER AND OVER. Why did the 2nd level unlock if it's impossible to beat? It's a shame to give this a negative review. The concept and the artwork and such are all cool. I didn't get to play before they revamped the meta progression system, but as a new player I can say that the current one feels really bad. I beat hell 2 and kingdom 3 and that's as far as I can get despite trying different strategies and being as patient as I can feasibly be to work my way up to tackling higher tiers of units before they're thrown at me at the different minute mark events. I near enough have maxed out the small skill tree that remains (unless some secret extra skill nodes are going to appear), and the only way to actually buff my minions is grinding out thousands of kills to complete scaling achievement milestones that come with upgrades like "+2% attack speed" or "+2% health" that after however many thousand more kills goes up to a massive +4% and so on. It's not fun to need to mindlessly grind those out for hours and hours on a difficulty that isn't a challenge just so I have a slim chance of succeeding against the next level that's currently way too much of a challenge.

There's a terrible lack of necromany games in the world, let alone good ones, and this game fits nicely into the "comically large swarm of Dudes" category. Minion AI and aggro range is pretty weak, the upgrades and powers lack oomph and there's an overall lack of variety in enemies, spells and locations (which will probably change over time, it's not done yet) but it's hard to beat the joy of just having a screen full of Evil Little Fellows swarming around and beating up peasants The only real problem for me is the dialogue; the game goes hard into some kind of dom/mommy/BDSM vibe, and it is unavoidable. Every line of dialogue has a chance to either be evil and slayful, or horny and awkward. I get second hand embarrassment from a lot of them. If that's what you're into then whatever, but if you're not, just mute the voices and try not to look at the subtitles
